<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

The review of #71 (plan 179, merged 2026-10-28 as 077d383) found that `SendOutcome::Retry` calls `queue.retry(id, 100ms)`, which truncates to whole seconds, so `not_before = now` and the 250 ms loop retries at once, with no attempt cap and the 429 `retry_after` ignored. `run_once` returns before `poll_inbound()` on a Retry, so Jordan's Telegram messages to pij are not picked up while any outbound job retries. `reqwest::Client::new()` has no timeout, so a stalled upload hangs the worker. The daemon producer's body + multi-file path has no hermetic test (a mutant that drops the body survives shim_http). Nits N1-N4 are in #77. Rulings: assets/rulings.md.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- A failing Telegram send backs off, honours retry_after and eventually gives up on the record.
- Inbound Telegram messages are never starved by outbound trouble.
- The producer's body + files path is proven hermetically.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Saving inbound media to disk (#70).
- Changing which API method a file uses.
- The legacy TS telegram bridge.

<a id="acceptance-criteria"></a>

## Acceptance criteria

| id | claim | state | note | receipt | pressure | proven_by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ac-0001 | Backoff. A Retry outcome is rescheduled with per-attempt exponential backoff with a cap, honours a 429's `parameters.retry_after` when longer, and never schedules a retry sooner than requested (fix the whole-second truncation in crates/store/src/queue.rs retry, or carry milliseconds). After a bounded number of attempts (or a bounded age) the job fails terminally with the reason recorded and an event appended. Body→files order on a serial key is preserved explicitly, not by the 0 s truncation. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | [lg-0002](assets/execution-log.dd.md#entries) |
| ac-0002 | Inbound never starves. `poll_inbound` runs every tick whatever the outbound job did (Retry, failure, success). A test holds an outbound job in Retry and shows an inbound update is delivered to the bound seat within one poll. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | [lg-0003](assets/execution-log.dd.md#entries) |
| ac-0003 | Request timeouts. The Telegram HTTP client has a connect timeout and a send timeout sized for a 50 MB upload on a slow link (state the numbers and why). A stalled upload ends as a Retry, not a hung worker, and inbound keeps polling meanwhile. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | [lg-0003](assets/execution-log.dd.md#entries) |
| ac-0004 | Hermetic producer test (S2). A shim_http-style test posts `/v1/sidecar` `telegram_document` with a body and two files and asserts body-first order and `#1`/`#2` ids, with no real tmux. The review's mutant X2 (the producer drops the body) dies. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | [lg-0004](assets/execution-log.dd.md#entries) |
| ac-0005 | Nits. N1: a reused `--msg-id` with different content is refused by name (or returns the live job's actual document), never a receipt for bytes that will not be sent, and leaves no orphan copy. N2: a failed job's staged copies are removed after a stated retention, by a sweep that launches nothing and runs rarely (state its cadence). N3: enqueue of body+files is one transaction, or the docs say exactly what an internal error leaves queued. N4: the CLI and shim name a symlinked `--file` the same way. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | [lg-0004](assets/execution-log.dd.md#entries) |
| ac-0006 | Cost (AGENTS.md § Resource cost). State the retry loop's steady-state cost: HTTP calls per minute for a job that keeps failing, CPU while idle, and that no process is launched. A test counts calls over a simulated window. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0002](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | [lg-0005](assets/execution-log.dd.md#entries) |
